prompt: A hospital's supply costs rose 18% in two years. Patient volumes and the number of items used per patient were both flat. Which is the strongest initial hypothesis?

options.text: Doctors are probably using more supplies per patient than before.
options.feedback: Items used per patient were flat.

options.text: A rise in patient numbers is likely driving the extra spend.
The hospital is probably paying more per item than it did two years ago.
options.feedback: Right. With volume and usage flat, the price paid per item must have risen. I'd compare unit prices for the top supplies with contract prices.

options.text: Supply spending has probably drifted out of control.
options.feedback: Too vague to test: drifted how, and what data would show it?

explanation: The data shows spend up 18% with patients and items per patient flat, so the price paid per item rose. Likely cause: buying off-contract. To test it, compare unit prices paid for the top supplies with contract prices. If they match, the contract prices themselves went up.
